why: ticfac keeps its run state in the repository it executes against, under
.ticfac/ (SPEC 10.4). This file pins three things that two implementations
have to agree on before either exists: the LAYOUT (which record lives at
which path, and which paths are gitignored exhaust), the PERSISTENCE POLICY
(durable means pushed on origin; churn stays on the run branch; the terminal
record lands once at publish; the run branch is tagged at terminal state),
and the COMPARE-AND-SWAP RULES that make an effect idempotent (SPEC 4.2:
create-if-absent for a dispatch, SHA-guarded update for a checkpoint, both
against the ORIGIN ref).
Why it needs two readers rather than a paragraph in the spec: the same rules
are reached through two entirely different mechanisms. A local host does
create-if-absent and SHA-guarded update with `git push --force-with-lease`;
a Cloudflare Worker does them through the GitHub contents API, which is a
compare-and-swap on the branch ref. Two mechanisms implementing one rule is
exactly the shape that drifts silently, and the failure is invisible in the
worst way: a CAS that has quietly stopped guarding does not error, it lets a
second reconciler dispatch the same attempt twice and pays for both.
So the cas.sequences below are not prose. They are executable table tests,
run on both sides against an in-memory git fake, and a fake that disagrees
with the fixture is a reconciler that would disagree with git.

layout.why_one_file_per_record: Concurrent EpicRuns writing different runs/<id>/ directories merge cleanly — the same argument ticks makes for one file per tick.

entries.why: One commit per state change. Recovery is a fetch; audit is the log of this path.

entries.name_is: <n> is the 1-based attempt number for the tick
entries.why: Existence IS the idempotency marker: a second reconciler racing the same attempt is refused by the repository, not by a lock it might have lost.

entries.name_is: <key> is the record's own `key` field, and names the evidence: stable for the same check on the same source ref
entries.written_on: a configured command or check producing a result
entries.why: Evidence is a bounded, redacted record of something that already happened (SPEC 10.1). A record that can be overwritten is not evidence.

entries.name_is: <n> is the 1-based decision number within the run
entries.why: The request and the validated response land together, with provenance, so a decision can be re-read without re-asking a model.
A derived index over the run directories. Rebuildable from the committed records, so it is never the authority and never merged.
Exhaust. Useful while a run is live, worthless afterwards, and far too noisy to commit at a run's write cadence.

authority.durable_authority: the committed records under .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/, on origin
authority.why: SPEC 12 Phase 0 step 6: run state never lands in D1 as authority. A hosted index is a cache that a fetch can rebuild; if it were the authority, a run's record would be unreadable from the repository it ran against.

boundary.why_default: The coordination key is already repository + target ref.

persistence.why_origin: The writer is a sandbox that can be wiped. A container that dies leaves its work on origin or nowhere.

terminal_record.form: final form only: the last checkpoint, all attempts, evidence and decisions

tag.why: The full history stays reachable for a post-mortem without living in the target's log — and a failed or cancelled run's history is as reachable as a successful one's.

fragment: # .ticfac/runs/** is COMMITTED — it is the run's durable record (SPEC 10.4),
# and durable means pushed on origin. Only these two are exhaust:

envelope.why: SPEC 10.4: every committed file carries a schema_version and the provenance fields of an evidence record. That is what makes one loose JSON file readable years later by something that did not write it.
envelope.provenance_is: the $defs.provenance object of contracts/job-protocol.json, copied here field for field so the local $refs resolve. It is the SAME object, not a compatible one: the cross-file readers compare the two definitions structurally, because two spellings of one shape is what bundle 1.2.0 shipped.

evidence.why: A record this contract PLACES but does not DEFINE. Bundle 1.2.0 defined the evidence record twice — flat and closed there, nested and open here — and no document could satisfy both; neither suite saw it, because each validated its own examples against its own schema. There is now one definition, and this is the pointer to it.
evidence.division_of_labour: This contract owns WHERE the file goes (.ticfac/runs/<run-id>/evidence/<key>.json), HOW it is written (create-if-absent against origin) and that it carries the envelope; job-protocol.json owns WHAT IS IN IT. The golden and invalid examples below are validated against that definition, from both readers.
evidence.key_is: the <key> in the path is the record's own `key` field, so a filename and a citation in a JobResult name the same thing

provenance.description: Where a record came from: which run, which refs, which phase, and what produced it — SPEC §10.1's provenance fields. This is the ONE definition of them in the bundle. The evidence record below carries it, and so does every committed .ticfac/ record (contracts/ticfac-run-state.json, SPEC §10.4: 'every committed file carries a schema_version and the provenance fields of an evidence record'). Every field is REQUIRED, nullable where it can be genuinely absent: a record that omits integration_ref and one that states it as null are different claims, and only the second is evidence.

tick_id.description: Null for epic-level or run-level records.

attempt.description: Null for a record that belongs to no single dispatch — a run checkpoint, say.

integration_ref.description: Null before integration. Required-and-null rather than omitted, because 'this ran before integration' and 'nobody recorded where it ran' are different claims.

executor.description: Null for a record no executor produced — a reconciler-side decision, say.

backend.description: The concrete backend, e.g. container-shell. Backend names do not cross the JobSpec seam; a record names them AFTER the fact, which is how a run is explained without the reconciler ever choosing one.

role.description: Null for a deterministic check with no LLM behind it — a test command is evidence too.

phase.$comment: The gate vocabulary the current implementation already runs (SPEC §6.1 Gates: 'configured worker/post-wave/integrated/review commands'), plus closeout. Naming the phase is what makes a record reproducible: the same command against the same ref at a different phase answers a different question. Reached through $defs.provenance, so a checkpoint, an attempt, a decision and an evidence record all name their phase from this one closed vocabulary.

executor.$comment: SPEC §4.3 initial executors. An executor NAME crosses this seam; a concrete backend name does not — that is the difference between `cloudflare-computer` here and `container-shell` in an evidence record, which explains a run after the fact.

role.description: SPEC §4.4. There is no universal Decision Agent: every LLM call is a bounded job with a role-specific contract, so the role is a closed vocabulary rather than free text.

checkpoint.$comment: One per run, at .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/checkpoint.json. Updated under a SHA guard; written on state change, never on observation.

sequence.description: Monotonic within the run, incremented on each state change. A checkpoint whose sequence did not move is an observation, and an observation writes nothing.

reason.description: What changed. Present because a checkpoint is written on a state change, so there is always something to name.

attempt.$comment: One per dispatch, at .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/attempts/<n>.json. Created if absent — its existence is the idempotency marker for the dispatch.

job_handle.$comment: The JobHandle returned by the executor's start (SPEC 4.3). Its shape is owned by the executor-protocol contract, not by this one — this contract only requires that the handle a dispatch was made with is recorded beside the marker that proves the dispatch happened.

decision.$comment: One per role-job exchange, at .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/decisions/<n>.json. Created if absent.

response.$comment: The role-result record. Its shape is owned by the role-result contract; what this contract pins is that the VALIDATED response is what lands, with provenance, so the decision can be re-read without re-asking a model.

checkpoint.reason: wave 1 fan-in complete: 4 of 4 ticks reported

request.question: wave 1 is green; is the frontier ready for wave 2?

response.reason: 8jz depends on the Phase 0 schemas landing first

invalid.why: no provenance — SPEC 10.4 requires it on every committed file, and a checkpoint that does not name the source sha it reconciled cannot be replayed
a state nobody agreed to: 'in_flight' is not in the enum, and a state meaning 'in flight' that no other reconciler can settle is the exact failure this vocabulary is closed to prevent
invalid.expect_error_contains: $.state: in_flight is not one of the permitted values

invalid.why: no job_handle — the marker proves a dispatch happened, and without the handle nothing can inspect, cancel or collect the job it started
attempt is a string — <n> in the path is a number and a record whose attempt is "2" cannot be compared to one whose attempt is 2
no validated flag — an unvalidated model response landing as a decision is how a hallucinated wave gets dispatched

provenance without integration_ref — evidence that does not name the ref it was produced against proves nothing about the ref being gated. Refused by the referenced definition (references.evidence), not by a second schema kept here.

THE DOCUMENT BUNDLE 1.2.0 SHIPPED AS THIS CONTRACT'S GOLDEN EVIDENCE EXAMPLE. It carried a bare `command` string, an `output_uri`, no `check` and an acceptance of "accepted", and it validated here because this contract's envelope was open past schema_version, key and provenance — while job-protocol.json's records.evidence refused it 22 ways. Kept as the negative control for the reconciliation: the open envelope is gone, and the shape that only ever validated against half the bundle is now refused by the half that defines the record.

why: SPEC 4.2: an effect is idempotent when the compare-and-swap that precedes
it proves it has not already happened. Two modes, and each record kind
gets exactly one of them.
The guard is against the ORIGIN ref. A local host reaches it with
`git push --force-with-lease`; a Worker reaches it through the GitHub
contents API, which is a compare-and-swap on the branch ref. The signal
funnel already relies on the second of those.

mechanisms.worker: the GitHub contents API (a compare-and-swap on the branch ref)

modes.guard: the path must not exist on the origin ref
modes.why: The file's existence is the proof the effect already happened. A refused create means another reconciler already dispatched, so this one must not.

modes.guard: the blob sha on the origin ref must equal the one the writer fetched
modes.why: A conflict means the writer's view of the run is stale — someone else advanced it. Re-fetch and reconcile from what is actually there; never retry blindly.

fake.why: A tiny in-memory model of the one git behaviour these rules depend on, so the sequences below are executable in any language without a repository. Origin is shared; each actor has its own fetched VIEW of it, which is the only thing its SHA guard may use.

ops.does: actor.view := the current origin path->sha map
a poll that learns nothing: refreshes the view and writes nothing
write into the actor's local tree only; origin is untouched
commit and push in one operation, guarded on the path being absent from origin
commit and push in one operation, guarded on origin's sha for the path equalling the actor's fetched sha

rules: A successful push refreshes the WRITER's view of the path it wrote, and no other actor's.
A refused push writes nothing: origin_writes does not move.
update_if_sha with no fetched sha for the path is conflict_missing_base — a writer that never read origin cannot compare against it.
commit_local never changes origin. Durable means pushed.

sequences.why: Two reconcilers race the same dispatch. The second is refused by the repository, not by a lock it might have lost — and the loser must NOT start a job.

Attempt 2 is a different path, so a retry is never blocked by attempt 1. And a reconciler that died after dispatching and restarts replays the same create — which is refused, so the job is not started twice.
The first checkpoint is a create; every later one is guarded on the sha the writer fetched. A reconciler holding a stale view is refused, re-fetches, and reconciles from what is actually there.

A reconciler that never fetched has no origin sha to compare against, so its update is refused rather than silently overwriting. This is the rule that makes 'the compare-and-swap is against the origin ref, not the local one' testable.
The lesson of the sandbox keeper: a container that dies leaves its work on origin or nowhere. A checkpoint that exists only in a working tree or a local commit does not exist.
Checkpoint on state change, not on observation. A poll that learns nothing writes nothing — at ten checkpoints an hour the cost is negligible, and at one commit per poll it is not.
Evidence is a record of something that already happened, and a validated decision is a thing a model was paid for once. Both are create-if-absent, so a replay after a restart cannot overwrite either.
